headline: Tech stocks surge on AI tailwinds while PLS.AX jumps 4% on dividend news — and the Iran conflict hits six months with no end in sight.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a strong session today, jumping 4.1% after the company released a dividend update that sparked renewed interest. Lithium sentiment appears to be turning — analysts at Kalkine noted the move may signal a broader shift in how the market is pricing lithium stocks. Still down 20% overall on your position, but today's move is a meaningful green shoot.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG rose 1.9% last night — Google's cloud revenue continues to grow strongly, helping it hold its own against Microsoft and Amazon in the AI race. Analysts also highlighted that Alphabet weathered heavy AI spending (capex) well after a Q2 earnings beat, which has kept investor confidence solid.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT climbed 1.6% last night, and is now up 12% since its last earnings report. The catalyst continues to be AI momentum — Microsoft announced a 50MW AI compute buildout in North America, signalling it's doubling down on infrastructure to meet surging demand.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO was basically flat last night, edging up just 0.1%. The real news is the GTA 6 preview — analysts at CNBC are calling it a blockbuster demand signal, and early footage has the gaming world buzzing. The long-term story here remains intact: GTA 6 is shaping up to be one of the biggest game launches in history.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: No ASX price data available for today's close — VDHG didn't record a tradeable price today. As a diversified high-growth ETF, it tracks a broad mix of global and Aussie shares, so last night's modest dip on US markets would have a mild drag when it next prices.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: No price data for VGE today. Emerging markets are being watched closely as the Iran war at six months creates ongoing uncertainty in the Middle East, which can ripple into energy-dependent emerging economies.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: No price data for VTS today. The underlying US market slipped modestly last night (S&P 500 down 0.25%, NASDAQ down 0.48%), but this is minor noise — the long-term US total market story remains strong.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: No price data for GXAI today. The broader AI theme is very much alive — news today of 100+ tech companies (including OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic) calling for urgent action on AI security threats keeps AI front-and-centre as a growth story.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Strong day, but still deep in the red overall
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped 4.1% today on a dividend update and improving lithium sentiment. That's encouraging, but your position is still down about 20% overall (-$30.71 AUD). Nothing structurally broken here — lithium demand for batteries remains a long-term story. Sit tight and let it recover.

watch_today.title: MSFT — AI infrastructure push keeps the momentum going
watch_today.detail: Microsoft rose 1.6% last night and is up 12% since its last earnings report. The 50MW AI compute buildout announced this week shows the company is investing heavily in staying ahead. You're up 15.8% on this position. No reason to change anything — this is exactly the kind of long-term compounder you want to hold.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 buzz building ahead of launch
watch_today.detail: Take-Two was flat last night but the real story is GTA 6. A new preview has analysts calling it a blockbuster demand signal, and the game's cyberleaks are keeping it in the headlines. Your position is barely in profit (+0.48%), but the thesis is firmly intact — GTA 6 could be a major catalyst when it drops.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike — could be coming in September
watch_today.detail: Three of Australia's major banks have now flipped their forecasts and are predicting at least one more RBA rate hike in 2026. Rising household spending data is adding pressure. A rate hike would be bad news for property, but could push the AUD higher. Watch for any RBA commentary next week.

watch_today.title: GOOG — Cloud strength a positive long-term signal
watch_today.detail: Alphabet rose 1.9% last night, with analysts highlighting growing cloud revenue as a key differentiator against Microsoft and Amazon. Your position is up 11.9% overall. The AI investment story is intact — hold confidently.

watch_today.title: Gold drops sharply — markets settling into Iran war 'new normal'
watch_today.detail: Gold fell 2.1% last night to around US$4,511/oz. After six months of the Iran conflict, markets appear to be pricing in a prolonged stalemate rather than escalation — reducing the 'fear premium' in gold. Oil also dipped slightly to US$83.29. Worth watching if tensions shift.

world.summary: The dominant global story is the Iran war hitting its six-month mark with no resolution in sight, reshaping Middle East geopolitics and energy markets. Meanwhile, US election integrity is under fire as Trump's mail voting restrictions face repeated court blocks.

stories.title: Iran War: Six Months In — Markets Adapt, Region Transformed
stories.why_it_matters: The war between the US/Israel and Iran has now been grinding on for six months, and global financial markets have largely stopped panicking — pricing in a long stalemate rather than an escalating crisis. The Council on Foreign Relations notes the conflict has fundamentally reshaped the US's relationship with the Middle East and transformed regional power dynamics. Regional powers are quietly seeking an 'off-ramp' to end hostilities, but no ceasefire is imminent. For everyday Australians, the key impact is energy prices — oil has stayed elevated but stable around US$83/barrel.

stories.title: Trump's Mail Voting Crackdown Blocked by Courts — Again
stories.why_it_matters: A federal judge has again halted Trump's executive order that would have restricted mail-in voting ahead of the US midterm elections — that's two blocks now on the same order. The rules would have required new postal service restrictions that critics say would make it harder for millions of Americans, particularly the elderly and rural voters, to cast ballots by mail. Axios reports Trump is pulling every lever available to reshape how US elections work. This is a significant constitutional battle with implications for November's midterms.

stories.title: Middle East Conflict Creates Energy Winners and Losers
stories.why_it_matters: Bloomberg has mapped out which countries and companies are winning and losing from the ongoing Iran conflict's impact on energy markets. The Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which about 20% of the world's oil flows — remains a flashpoint, though the US argues new pipeline routes could make it less critical. Energy experts disagree, saying there's no realistic short-term alternative. Higher energy costs flow through to petrol prices and inflation globally, including in Australia.

stories.title: Trump's Strength in Primaries Clear — Midterms a Different Test
stories.why_it_matters: The New York Times analysis shows Trump has performed strongly in Republican primaries across the country, but the upcoming November midterms are a very different challenge — turnout patterns, swing districts, and independent voters all shift the calculus. The results will determine control of the House and Senate, which directly affects whether Trump can push through his economic agenda (tariffs, tax changes, spending cuts) — all of which have global market implications including for Australia.

stories.title: Thai Airways Cracks the World's Top 10 Airlines for 2026
stories.why_it_matters: Thai Airways has broken into the world's top 10 airlines for 2026 — a notable comeback story given the carrier went through bankruptcy restructuring just a few years ago. For Australian travellers, particularly those flying through Bangkok as a hub to Europe or Asia, this is good news: top-10 ranked airlines typically offer better service, newer fleets, and stronger route networks. It's a reminder that Asian aviation is bouncing back strongly post-pandemic.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street, US markets slipped modestly — the S&P 500 dipped 0.25% and the NASDAQ fell 0.48% — but your individual tech holdings bucked the trend, with GOOG and MSFT both rising solidly. Gold had its worst night in a while, dropping 2.1%, as markets seem to be settling into the Iran war stalemate rather than pricing in escalation. The ASX 200 didn't return a closing price in today's data. The Aussie dollar eased slightly to US71.64¢.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Slight pull-back last night — modest profit-taking after recent gains.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech index dipped slightly last night, though GOOG and MSFT both rose against the trend.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: No closing price recorded in today's data.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil barely moved — markets are treating the Iran conflict as a stable stalemate for now.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold dropped sharply — down 2.1% — as the 'fear premium' from the Iran war fades with markets pricing in a prolonged stalemate.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar eased slightly. RBA rate hike speculation is actually lifting it somewhat, but broader USD strength is a counterforce.

politics.summary: The big domestic story is interest rates — three major banks have now flipped their forecasts and expect the RBA to raise rates at least once more in 2026, likely in September. Rising household spending data is adding fuel to the fire, and the impact on home buyers and sellers is real.

stories.title: Three Major Banks Now Predict Another RBA Rate Hike in 2026
stories.why_it_matters: ANZ, Westpac, and NAB have all reversed their earlier predictions and now expect the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) to raise interest rates at least one more time before the end of 2026, with September the most likely timing. This comes after data showed household spending rising faster than expected — meaning Australians are still spending, which keeps inflation pressure alive. For anyone with a mortgage or looking to buy property, this is a significant development: higher rates mean bigger repayments.

stories.title: Rising Household Spending Heaps Pressure on Labor and RBA
stories.why_it_matters: New data shows Australian household spending is rising sharply, which puts the Labor government and the RBA in a tough spot. Labor wants to claim cost-of-living relief is working, but the spending data suggests consumers are still active — which could mean inflation stays sticky. The RBA's job is to cool inflation, and if spending doesn't slow down, another rate hike becomes more likely. It's a political headache for Albanese as well as a financial one for mortgage holders.

stories.title: September Rate Hike Fears Add to Uncertainty for Home Buyers and Sellers
stories.why_it_matters: Domain reports that the prospect of a September RBA rate hike is already freezing up parts of the property market — buyers are pausing, and sellers are uncertain whether now is the right time to list. Sydney and Melbourne auction clearance rates have softened. For Gold Coast property holders, the uncertainty adds to an already-complex market. If the RBA does hike, expect further cooling in auction activity through spring.

stories.title: Australian Dollar Rises as RBA Rate Hike Odds Increase
stories.why_it_matters: Traders are pricing in a higher chance of an RBA rate hike, and that's actually pushing the Australian dollar up slightly — higher interest rates tend to attract foreign money into Australian dollar deposits, which lifts the currency. A stronger Aussie dollar is a mixed bag: it's good for Australians travelling or buying US shares, but it slightly reduces the AUD value of your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) when converted back.

ai.summary: The headline AI story today is a major industry-wide warning: over 100 tech companies including OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Microsoft have jointly called for urgent government action to defend against AI-powered cyberattacks — saying the window to act is narrowing fast.

stories.title: 100+ Tech Giants Warn of AI Cyberattack Threat — 'Window to Act is Narrowing'
stories.why_it_matters: More than 100 companies — including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft — have signed a joint statement warning that AI is rapidly becoming a tool for sophisticated cyberattacks, and that governments and companies have a 'limited window' to build defences before it's too late. The letter calls for urgent regulatory action, better security standards, and international coordination. In plain terms: the same AI tools that can write code, summarise documents, or generate images can also be weaponised to hack systems at a scale and speed humans can't match. For investors in AI-exposed stocks like GOOG and GXAI.AX, this highlights both the risk and the regulatory scrutiny ahead.

stories.title: Bill Gates Reverses on AI Regulation — Says Industry Has 'Crossed Safety Lines'
stories.why_it_matters: Bill Gates — who previously argued against heavy AI regulation — has publicly reversed his position, now saying the tech industry has crossed important safety lines and that stronger guardrails are needed. Gates has reportedly gone quiet on specifics, but the reversal from one of tech's most prominent figures is significant. It adds to growing momentum for governments to step in and regulate AI development before the risks outpace the safeguards.

stories.title: Microsoft Launches 50MW AI Compute Buildout in North America
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft has announced it is building 50 megawatts of new AI compute infrastructure in North America — essentially massive data centres dedicated to running AI models. To put that in perspective, 50MW is enough electricity to power tens of thousands of homes. This signals Microsoft isn't just selling AI software, it's building the physical backbone to run it. Good news for MSFT holders — this kind of capital investment usually precedes a meaningful revenue ramp.

stories.title: APEC Pushes for Global AI Standards as Regulation Debate Heats Up
stories.why_it_matters: APEC — the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, which includes Australia, the US, China, and Japan — is now actively discussing the need for shared AI standards across member economies. As AI becomes embedded in finance, healthcare, and supply chains, having incompatible rules between countries creates real trade and compliance headaches. Australia's participation in shaping these standards matters for how local businesses can operate globally.

sport.summary: In the NRL, Penrith go back to the top of the ladder after a feisty win over Canterbury, while Manly kept their finals dream alive with a big victory. Melbourne Storm demolished the Broncos at Suncorp. In the AFL, finals are set and there's sadness with the passing of a footy legend.

stories.title: Panthers Climb to Top of NRL Ladder After Feisty Win Over Bulldogs (24-10)
stories.why_it_matters: Penrith Panthers beat the Canterbury Bulldogs 24-10 in a spiteful game at CommBank Stadium on Friday night, reclaiming top spot on the NRL ladder with just two rounds to go. Fox Sports described the Bulldogs as suffering a 'silly brain explosion' moment that effectively ended any lingering hope of making the finals — Canterbury's season is all but over. Panthers look ominous heading into the finals.

stories.title: Storm Thrash Broncos 46-20 at Suncorp — Brisbane's Form Alarm Bells Ring
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne Storm put on a clinic at Suncorp Stadium on Thursday night, demolishing the Brisbane Broncos 46-20. It was an emphatic performance from Storm, who remain serious finals contenders. For Gold Coast fans, it's a reminder of just how strong Melbourne's forward pack is — the result will do nothing for Brisbane's confidence heading into the pointy end of the season.

stories.title: Manly Sea Eagles Smash Dragons 44-10 to Keep Finals Hopes Alive
stories.why_it_matters: The Sea Eagles were ruthless at 4 Pines Park on Friday night, running over St George Illawarra 44-10. The big win keeps Manly firmly in the finals race heading into Round 26's remaining games. The Dragons, meanwhile, are in serious trouble at the wrong end of the table.

stories.title: AFL Finals Set — All 10 Teams Can Win, But Blues Reality is Stark
stories.why_it_matters: The 2026 AFL finals field is set, and both Fox Sports and The Guardian have run deep dives on why every team can — and can't — go all the way. The stand-out storyline is Carlton (the Blues), whose finals path looks particularly difficult given form and fixture. Meanwhile, the Legends Game saw Buddy Franklin (Lance Franklin) go big for the Vics in what was reportedly a crowd-pleasing exhibition match.

stories.title: AFL World Mourns Sudden Death of Footy Legend
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL community is mourning the sudden death of a footy legend — Yahoo News reports the passing has prompted an outpouring of tributes, with the phrase 'never forgotten' echoing across the football world. The article doesn't name the individual, but the response suggests someone deeply significant to the game. A sad day for Australian football.
